title: GPU idle fragmentation snapshot and utilization notes
summary: Daily export focused on idle fragmentation across pools and clusters. This snapshot complements fleet-level utilization exports by surfacing small, widely-distributed free GPU slices that block consolidation. Goal: inform short-term defragmentation and scheduling knobs to recover 3-5% effective capacity without adding hardware.

observations: 1) Idle fragmentation (idle_frag_pct) correlates with high p95_util spreads in pools with many small jobs (see cl-olive-03, cl-sable-09). 2) Pools with reserved_slots > 0 sometimes show higher free_idle_gpus due to mismatched reservation sizes (cl-amber-01 reserved 16 but 9 free idle GPUs). 3) Training-heavy pools show nightly fragmentation from many small warmup jobs; potential for job packing + short-term bin-packing heuristics. 4) Experimental clusters have low fragmentation but high tail latency — suggests transient queuing, not resource holes.
recommended_actions: - Short: enable opportunistic packing for low-priority pools (target cl-olive-03, cl-sable-09) for next 7 days; monitor queue latency. - Mid: add a nightly defragmentation job that drains small ephemeral slots into a staging pool and relaunches bigger jobs to free contiguous GPUs. - Long: scheduler change to prefer contiguous allocation for single-node multi-GPU jobs and add fragmentation metric to autoscaler heuristics. - Ops: add alert when free_idle_gpus > 10% and p95_util - avg_util > 25 to trigger manual review.
